text:
I need to verify the historical fact about Hans Holbein the Younger's role as court painter.

Hans Holbein the Younger (c. 1497-1543) was a German-Swiss artist who became court painter to Henry VIII of England. He is famous for his portraits of Henry VIII and members of his court. Holbein first visited England in 1526-1528, returned in 1532, and was appointed the King's Painter to Henry VIII around 1536, serving in this capacity until his death in 1543.

All four agents agree on Henry VIII with very high confidence (0.98-1.00), and this aligns perfectly with the well-documented historical record. This is one of the most famous artist-patron relationships in English history.

Answer: Henry VIII
Confidence: 0.99
